title: China AI Stocks Sink as US Chip Curbs Hit Labs and Hyperscalers
html:
(Bloomberg) -- Chinese artificial-intelligence stocks tumbled Tuesday after the US moved to further restrict access to advanced chips, with the country's biggest hyperscalers and AI model developers among the hardest hit.

Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. shares dropped as much as 5.6% in Hong Kong while Baidu Inc.'s tumbled 6.6%, helping drag the Hang Seng Tech Index down 2.3%. AI model pure plays Minimax Group Inc. and Z.AI Co., or Zhipu, fell more than 6% each, while robot maker Yushu Technology Co. sank as much as 11% in Shanghai.

The broad selloff underscores how tighter US restrictions threaten multiple layers of China's AI industry, from cloud giants supplying computing power to model developers racing to catch up with US rivals. The proposed rules could raise the cost of accessing advanced compute and close off overseas routes Chinese firms have used to work around existing restrictions.

"We see this as a negative development for China's AI cloud industry, as tighter access to advanced computing resources could constrain AI model training and slow cloud revenue growth," Nomura Holdings Inc. analysts Jialong Shi and Rachel Guo wrote in a note.

The draft regulation would require data center operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil to obtain a US government license before exporting advanced chips to customers in those countries. That would go a step beyond existing restrictions that prevent Chinese tech firms from directly buying some of the most advanced US chips.

The new rule was released days after Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia's chief executive officer following his admission to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Tech investors remain on edge with key earnings also due this week from Nvidia as well as Alibaba and Tencent Holdings Ltd.

"The curbs add a concrete risk to revenues and access to computing capacity, but they are landing in a market already nervous about AI valuations, spending returns and Nvidia's leadership outlook," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Markets. "This is a meaningful escalation."

The fallout extended beyond China. Samsung Electronics Co. fell as much as 3.3% and Advantest Corp. slid 6.3%, extending losses among Asian technology hardware shares already under pressure from the turmoil surrounding Nvidia and persistent concerns over AI financing.
summary: Chinese artificial-intelligence stocks tumbled Tuesday after the US moved to further restrict access to advanced chips, with the country’s biggest hyperscalers and AI model developers among the hardest hit.
